text:
Marina: FWIW I prototyped a \"solo-primary\" mode idea this morning — per-tenant toggle: one region is writable, others serve reads and async replicate. Intended to simplify legal residency + active/active complexity. Thoughts?

Jae: can you sketch the failure modes? e.g., what happens if the solo primary goes down mid-write?

Marina: good q — plan was a lease + short TTL on the primary. If primary loses heartbeats we mark it read-only and promote standby after handshake. Promotion requires commit-log catch-up.

Priya: handshake + catch-up sounds like the usual headache. Do we have a plan for partially replicated tensors/kv state? atomicity?

Marina: minimal promise: writes that ack'd on primary remain authoritative. We use per-tenant WAL that other regions tail; promotion waits for WAL offset >= acked-offsets. Not trying to be AP here, it's intentionally a simpler single-writer model.

Aaron: how does this affect client routing? app teams expect low-latency writes from EU users — would they need to talk to EU primary always?

Marina: yes, UX is per-tenant residency: if tenant opts EU-solo-primary, clients should hit EU for writes. We provide client hints in responses and a lightweight redirect header for SDKs.

Lydia: redirect header worries me for non-SDK clients. DNS+anycast TTLs?

Marina: two options: 1) SDK client-level redirect using X-Redwood-Write-Endpoint, or 2) recommend region-pref DNS entries (short TTL ~30s) with traffic steering. both supported.

ryan: what about failover ordering? if primary goes flaky we can't just promote arbitrary standby. Need a safe promotion algorithm and operator approval flow.

Marina: agreed. suggested flow: detect lease expiry -> attempt auto-promotion if WAL lag < threshold and telemetry OK -> otherwise mark tenant \"degraded\" and page oncall with manual-promote option. Promotion always requires a final fencing check.

Priya: fencing check = ensure old primary cannot later accept writes, right? how do we enforce that if customer networks partition?

Jae: we enforce with a short-lived cluster lease recorded in global control-plane (signed token). old primary losing connectivity cannot renew lease; once control-plane issues new lease to standby, token revocation prevents old node from accepting writes. Need KMS-backed signing.

Aaron: operational complexity aside, how does this interact with caching layers (prefix cache, KV cache)? Eviction, warmup?

Marina: on promote we plan to prewarm cache with hot prefixes from recent WAL and snapshot diffs. Eviction: a short grace period where reads are served from standby with slightly older data until warm. We'll expose a metric \"tenant_data_freshness_ms\".

Lydia: runbook suggestion: include explicit client-side retry guidance and a one-click rollback for toggling solo-primary off for a tenant. Also test with simulated partitions.

Marina: noted. I'll add to runbook.

deploy-bot: Marina pushed branch feature/solo-primary-toggle to staging (build #4823) :rocket:

ryan: let's schedule a chaos run next week focused on lease flaps and WAL lag thresholds. I can own the test harness.

Priya: one more: telemetry for legal/audit — we must export per-write residency tags for audits (region, primary-ts, ack-offset).

Marina: yep will add fields to audit log. Thanks everyone, I'll update the RFC doc and drop checklist into the runbook.
